free_tier.stated: No quota stated anywhere on the page — the docs grant each project a vhost and say nothing about a byte limit. Practically it is the same filesystem family as FRS (uploaded over the same SFTP), so expect the same discretionary 20-30 GB band.

egress.terms: 'Unlimited bandwidth for Open Source projects' (sourceforge.net/create). 'Our project web servers frequently handle more than 50M hits per day; we handle server scaling, caching, load balancing, and performance tuning.' Served through Cloudflare.

tooling: Same SFTP/SCP/rsync upload path as FRS but to /home/project-web/<unixname>/htdocs. Static files come back over plain HTTPS on <unixname>.sourceforge.io — no client, no API, just a web origin. Custom domains supported via the Custom VHOST service.
chaining: A second independent quota-less origin per project, free once you already have the project. Because it is a static web origin rather than a download mirror, it is the natural Cloudflare-fronted serving layer for anything in FRS: serves as the hot/serving tier while FRS holds the archive. N projects -> N vhosts.
limits_note: per-object-cap: none published (it is a web root, not an artefact store). Request-rate: none published. Retention: 'always-on' service, files persist while the project exists. Practical caveat: it is a web root — directory indexes are not guaranteed, so you index your own paths.
reliability_note: Probed live: https://libreoffice.sourceforge.io/ -> 200 with 134,123 bytes of real HTML; https://gimp.sourceforge.io/ -> 403 (project redirects elsewhere). https://gparted.sourceforge.io/ -> 302 to the project's own domain. Expect some projects to 403/302 depending on their custom-VHOST config; a fresh project should serve its own root.

evidence.proved: 'each project is provided the PROJECT.sourceforge.io subdomain'; 'frequently handle more than 50M hits per day'; SFTP path /home/project-web/PROJECT/htdocs
probe: GET -> 302 Location: https://gparted.org/ ; GET https://gimp.sourceforge.io/ -> 403
